# Results — Study 838 (HAC Necessity): the naive *t* lies, Newey-West doesn't

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). This is a **research-method demo**:
a pure Monte-Carlo simulation with no market data, no network, and no cache. We build a
mean-zero (null) daily return series carrying the serial correlation of an overlapping
formation window, then compare the rejection rate of the **naive i.i.d. OLS *t*** against the
**Newey-West (HAC) *t***. The synthetic core is deterministic under the config seed. Frozen
as-of 2026-06-30 (the simulation stamp — this is a sim study, so the "tape" is the config, not
a calendar month). Match the fingerprints to confirm you hold the same simulation.*

## Data stamp

| Simulation | Reps × Days | Window | NW lags | Fingerprint | Source |

Fingerprint `767e2ce61be1` — the simulation config (seed 838; 600 reps × 2,520 days; overlap
window 21; Newey-West Bartlett bandwidth 42; two-sided 5% critical value 1.96; planted-effect
mean 6e-4). Null-matrix content fingerprint `0c98419fb4d7`.

## The headline — a 21-day overlap, mean = 0 (so every rejection is a false positive)

On a series we *built* to have zero mean and the autocorrelation of a 21-day formation window:

| Quantity | Value | Reading |
|---|--:|---|
| Nominal false-positive rate (α) | **5.00%** | what a calibrated test should deliver |
| **NAIVE (i.i.d.) false-positive rate** | **64.3%** | Wilson95 [60.4%, 68.1%] — catastrophic over-rejection |
| **Newey-West (HAC) false-positive rate** | **9.5%** | Wilson95 [7.4%, 12.1%] — near nominal |
| Naive *t* SD under the null | **4.86** | vs the closed form √21 = **4.58** — the *t* is inflated ~4.6× |
| Newey-West *t* SD under the null | **1.18** | ≈ 1, as a calibrated statistic should be |

The naive *t* rejects a **true** null **64% of the time** — thirteen times the 5% it advertises —
because it treats 2,520 heavily-overlapping observations as if they were independent. The
closed-form inflation factor for a *K*-day overlap is exactly **√K**, and the simulated naive-*t*
SD (4.86) lands right on √21 (4.58). Newey-West, told about the autocorrelation, brings the
false-positive rate back to ~9.5% — a small residual finite-sample over-rejection (well documented
for HAC estimators), not the naive catastrophe.

## The control — switch the autocorrelation OFF and the pitfall vanishes

A `window=1` overlap is just i.i.d. noise. Same generator, same estimators, only the serial
correlation removed:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| Naive false-positive rate | **5.67%** (back at nominal) |
| Newey-West false-positive rate | **6.83%** |
| Naive *t* SD | **1.01** (no inflation) |

The naive *t* is only dangerous *because of* the serial correlation — with i.i.d. data it is
perfectly calibrated. (Row-shuffling an already-drawn autocorrelated path is **not** a valid
placebo: the sample mean and SD are permutation-invariant, so the naive *t* would not move. The
cause has to be removed at generation — that is what `window=1` does.)

## Inflation vs the amount of autocorrelation

**Overlap window** (NW bandwidth = 2 × window):

| Window | Naive FP | NW FP | Naive *t* SD | √window |
|---:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 5.7% | 5.8% | 1.01 | 1.00 |
| 5 | 37.8% | 7.8% | 2.25 | 2.24 |
| 10 | 56.2% | 8.7% | 3.34 | 3.16 |
| 21 | 64.3% | 9.5% | 4.86 | 4.58 |
| 42 | 75.5% | 9.0% | 6.68 | 6.48 |
| 63 | 80.8% | 10.8% | 8.52 | 7.94 |

**AR(1)** (NW automatic bandwidth = 8):

| ρ | Naive FP | NW FP | Naive *t* SD | √((1+ρ)/(1−ρ)) |
|---:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 | 5.7% | 5.8% | 1.01 | 1.00 |
| 0.2 | 11.5% | 6.8% | 1.24 | 1.22 |
| 0.4 | 17.5% | 8.2% | 1.54 | 1.53 |
| 0.6 | 30.0% | 9.8% | 2.02 | 2.00 |
| 0.8 | 52.0% | 13.5% | 3.04 | 3.00 |

The empirical naive-*t* SD tracks the closed-form inflation factor to two figures across the
board. Note the AR(1) tail (ρ = 0.8): the *automatic* bandwidth of 8 lags is too small for that
much persistence, so even Newey-West drifts to 13.5% — a reminder that HAC needs an adequate
bandwidth, not merely the right formula.

## The positive control — the machinery still fires on a real effect

Plant a genuine daily mean of `6e-4` into the 21-day overlapping series (a true HAC *t* ≈ 3):

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| Newey-West rejection rate (power) | **89.2%** |
| Mean Newey-West *t* | **+3.42** |
| Share of NW *t* > 0 (correct sign) | **99.7%** |

Newey-West is not merely conservative — hand it a real effect and it rejects the null 89% of the
time, with the correct sign 99.7% of the time. The correction removes the *false* positives without
killing the *true* ones.

## The timer — there is, by construction, nothing to trade

Costing one null path as a notional daily long-short (one round-trip at 5 bps/side + 50 bps/yr
borrow): gross **+0.38 bps/day** (indistinguishable from zero), net **−9.76 bps/day**, or
**−24.6%** annualised. A null minus costs is a guaranteed loser — a Mirage by construction.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The series is a *constructed null*: its true mean is zero, so there is nothing
  real to find. Newey-West correctly declines to reject (9.5% ≈ nominal). No robust |*t*| ≥ 2 on any
  honest tape exists here because the honest tape is empty by design; the only thing that "rejects"
  is a broken estimator.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Nothing to harvest. The apparent significance the naive *t* manufactures
  is a standard-error artefact, not a return; costed, the null loses money.
- **Does ignoring autocorrelation fake significance? — CONFIRMED.** On a mean-zero tape the naive
  false-positive rate is **64%** (13× nominal), the naive *t* is inflated by exactly **√21 ≈ 4.6×**,
  the inflation tracks √window and √((1+ρ)/(1−ρ)) to two figures, the i.i.d. control is perfectly
  calibrated, and the Newey-West correction restores ~nominal error while still detecting a planted
  effect at 89% power. The pitfall is real, measurable, and correctable — report the HAC *t*, never
  the naive one, on any overlapping or serially-correlated series.
